In [[mathematics]], '''Pisier–Ringrose inequality''' is an inequality in the theory of C*-algebras which was proved by [[Gilles Pisier]] in 1978 affirming a conjecture of [[John Ringrose]]. It is an extension of the [[Grothendieck inequality]].

==Statement==
'''Theorem'''.<ref>{{harvtxt|Kadison|1993}}, Theorem&nbsp;D, p.&nbsp;60.</ref><ref>{{harvtxt|Pisier|1978}}, Corollary&nbsp;2.3, p.&nbsp;410.</ref> If <math>\gamma</math> is a bounded, linear mapping of one C*-algebra <math>\mathfrak{A}</math> into another C*-algebra <math>\mathfrak{B}</math>, then 
:<math>\left\|\sum_{j=1}^n \gamma(A_j)^* \gamma(A_j) + \gamma(A_j) \gamma(A_j)^*\right\| \le 4 \|\gamma \|^2 \left\| \sum_{j=1}^n A_j^*A_j + A_j A_j^* \right\|</math>
for each finite set <math>\{ A_1, A_2, \ldots, A_n \}</math> of elements <math>A_j</math> of <math>\mathfrak{A}</math>.
